title: A tool on the face
hook: A beak can interact with food in different ways.

knows: Birds have body structures and interact with their surroundings.
doesNotKnow: The short deep beak meets the seed between its upper and lower parts. The long narrow beak is shown probing a crevice. These are simplified examples, not a claim that beak shape alone determines every bird’s diet.

misconception: The observed arrangement has a different effect than the one shown.
objective: In the diagram, which beak is positioned to crack a hard seed?

claims.text: A beak can interact with food in different ways. In the diagram, which beak is positioned to crack a hard seed? The short deep beak meets the seed between its upper and lower parts. The long narrow beak is shown probing a crevice. These are simplified examples, not a claim that beak shape alone determines every bird’s diet.
claims.source: Unverified research starting point: OpenStax Biology 2e, Birds, https://openstax.org/books/biology-2e/pages/29-4-birds; species- or claim-specific citations require independent matching.

claims.text: The stage is a simplified schematic and the scenario is stipulated rather than observed.
Which illustrated tool resembles a beak that grips and cracks a seed? The stout jaws contact the seed from opposite sides.
